title: Frequency division in a 3-bit ripple counter
intro: The clock and the outputs Q0, Q1 and Q2 of a 3-bit negative-edge ripple counter (delays ignored), one clock period per step; then each output's period is marked.

elements.text: A ripple counter is a chain of divide-by-two stages

steps.caption: Clock period T. Q0 toggles at every falling edge of CLK; Q1 at every falling edge of Q0; Q2 at every falling edge of Q1.
Falling edge 2: the count becomes 010 = 2. Q0 has fallen, so Q1 toggles too.
Falling edge 4: the count becomes 100 = 4. Q0 has fallen, so Q1 toggles too. Q1 has fallen as well: Q2 toggles.
Falling edge 6: the count becomes 110 = 6. Q0 has fallen, so Q1 toggles too.
Falling edge 8: the count becomes 000 = 0. Q0 has fallen, so Q1 toggles too. Q1 has fallen as well: Q2 toggles.
Falling edge 10: the count becomes 010 = 2. Q0 has fallen, so Q1 toggles too.
Falling edge 12: the count becomes 100 = 4. Q0 has fallen, so Q1 toggles too. Q1 has fallen as well: Q2 toggles.
Q0 repeats every 2 clock periods: period 2T, frequency f/2.
Q1 repeats every 4 clock periods: period 4T, frequency f/4. Each stage halves the frequency of the one before.
Q2 repeats every 8 clock periods: period 8T, frequency f/8. The third stage is Q2, at f/8.
Stage i of a ripple counter runs at f/2^(i+1); an n-bit counter's last stage gives f/2^n, here f/8 with a 50% duty cycle.
